text:
marie: Quick heads-up — planning an admin-delegation dry-run next Tue (2026-07-12) to prune stale entitlements across org and projects. Goal: remove 90+ day inactive admin/owner roles, but this is a telemetry-first dry-run. I will not revoke anything until owners sign off. Please review the proposed scope below and flag any exceptions. /cc @kyle @jason @priya

kyle: Can you paste the exact query and the heuristics you’ll use to mark someone as inactive? We need to be careful about KMS grants and service-account bindings — those are easy to break.

marie: Query we’ll run (dry-run only):

```
SELECT principal, role, resource, last_active
FROM access_logs
WHERE role IN ('org/admin','project/owner','kms-admin')
  AND last_active < now() - interval '90 days';
```

Heuristics: last_active counts any authenticated token use (API or console). We’ll also attach a "prune_candidate" tag and cross-check with KMS grant map before any revoke. Dry-run will produce CSV + json report with tags: hold_kms_bindings, owner_confirmed, orphaned.

jason: Please ensure audit logs are retained for 180 days for any change and add a rollback plan. Also: do a canary group (10 principals + 1 non-prod project) where we actually revoke to validate fallout path.

priya: Oncall note — tie an alert to `admin-delegation-dryrun` in PagerDuty and add a short runbook. We should also snapshot IAM bindings and KMS policies before any action. If we revoke anyone, there must be a documented emergency restore flow.

marie: Runbook snippet (for the run):
1) Run query and generate `prune_report-{{ts}}.json`
2) Snapshot IAM: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy $PROJECT --format=json > /tmp/iam-snap-$PROJECT-$TS.json`
3) Snapshot KMS: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy $KEY --location=$LOC --keyring=$RING > /tmp/kms-snap-$KEY-$TS.json`
4) Notify resource owners (automated email + Slack thread) and wait 24h for objections
5) Apply oned-canary: revoke in `dev-canary` project, monitor 3h
6) If OK, schedule broader prune with staggered batches.

Also include the check for service-account key usage: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=$SA --filter="validAfterTime<$(date -d '90 days ago' --iso-8601=seconds)"`

sre-bot: Automated scan produced dry-run report: 47 candidates found. 3 candidates have active KMS grants not tied to project owners — svc-analytics@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com, svc-legacy@..., svc-backup@.... Full report: https://internal/reports/admin-prune/1809991233 :warning:

kyle: For those 3, exclude until owners confirm or we rotate keys. Also suggest running `./scripts/kms_grant_map.sh --project=redwood-core` to build mapping between principals and KMS grants; that script creates `kms-map-{{ts}}.csv`.

marie: Agreed — we'll tag them `hold_kms_bindings` in the report. Proposed timeline: Tue 15:00 UTC dry-run (generate report), Tue 18:00 UTC canary revoke in `dev-canary`, Wed 15:00 UTC broader prune if no regressions.

jason: Add a telemetry dashboard `entitlements-prune` with metrics: candidate_count, holds_count, successful_revokes, restore_actions, and an alert if auth failures spike >0.2% over 30m post-revoke. Also track per-role fallout (login failures by role).

priya: One more: any actual revoke must create a temporary recovery role `prune-recovery` with a documented and auditable elevate path and a 15-minute RTO to restore bindings. Put that in the runbook and in the PagerDuty play.

marie: Thanks all — I'll post the final target list and the dry-run export tomorrow morning. If you want to pre-review specific principals DM me or drop them into #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:

kyle: lgtm, will review the KMS mapping results once the script runs.

jason: I'll wire up the dashboard and alert rules before Tue so we can monitor the canary in real-time.

priya: I'll add the PagerDuty trigger and brief the oncall for Tue evening.

marie: Perfect. If anyone sees a principal that must be absolutely excluded, please reply here with the principal and reason.
